purpose: Collect a small set of genuine intraday sessions with recorded receipts so the v2.1.34 replay can measure data usability. Not a strategy, GEX or profitability study; no order is placed and no purchase is made by this file. v2.1.36 implements the collector and the multi-cycle assembler; no live session has been collected under it.

grounding.existing_command: python -m src.tools.capture_thetadata_once (one approved snapshot cycle per invocation; writes manifest, raw payloads, run intent and an attempt log with per-attempt receive times). The collector runs exactly this command once per slot with an explicit endpoint scope; its preflight, per-request authorisation, manifest and verification are unchanged.
grounding.normalizer: python -m src.tools.normalize_thetadata_capture (one capture directory per run, unchanged single-capture rule) and python -m src.tools.assemble_intraday_session (every executed cycle of one session, merged by recorded availability; implemented in v2.1.36)
grounding.collector: python -m src.tools.collect_intraday_session (dry run by default; --execute-live --approve <session approval>; --resume; --show-schedule DATE)
grounding.summary: python -m src.tools.summarize_intraday_pilot (several session readiness reports into one multi-session summary)

sessions.selection: Regular (non-early-close) trading sessions named in advance in the run intent; consecutive where possible so prior-session open interest is itself observed the day before.
sessions.calendar_check: /v3/calendar/on_date for each named session, recorded with the run intent.
sessions.preparation: The dry run must be taken on the session day (after midnight ET) because both approvals bind the market session date; the session approval additionally binds the schedule fingerprint, the request budget, the policy and the destination.

cycle.slots: One slot per cadence from the calendar open (09:30:00 ET) while the slot instant is before the calendar close: 09:30:00 .. 15:59:00 ET on a regular session (390 slots), 09:30:00 .. 12:59:00 ET on an early close (210 slots). The 09:29 first cycle of the v2.1.35 specification was outside the one-shot's capture window and is corrected, not overridden.

scopes.rule: FULL on the first slot and every refresh_every_seconds thereafter (09:30, 10:00, ..., 15:30 ET); MARKET otherwise.

cycle.alignment: One cycle in flight. A cycle may start until start_tolerance_seconds after its slot boundary. A cycle that spans later boundaries is recorded as overrunning; the slots it spans are recorded MISSED_OVERRUN and collection resumes at the next boundary still in the future. No overlap, no catch-up burst.
cycle.request_order_note: The order the existing request plan issues (verified against config/thetadata_intraday.yaml by test_the_intraday_profile_plans_the_specified_requests). The v2.1.35 specification listed Greeks before open interest; the pipeline has always issued open interest between the quote and Greeks requests, and the collector reuses the plan rather than reordering it. On the September 2 capture the quote and Greeks receipts were 1.08 s apart, inside the two-second skew budget; a MARKET cycle issues no open-interest request, so its quote and Greeks requests are adjacent.
cycle.why_quote_before_greeks: The Greeks endpoint re-reads quotes; issuing it after the quote request keeps the two market observations inside the two-second skew budget where the vendor allows.

requests.note: The pinned parameter max_dte is not documented as calendar or trading days; the replay applies its own 0-7 calendar-day filter regardless.
Model parameters are fixed in the run intent before the first request; the normalizer derives model_id from the verified request and never from a later choice.

requests.cadence: FULL slots: first cycle, then every refresh_every_seconds (30 minutes)
requests.note: OPRA publishes open interest around 06:30 ET for the prior session; repeated requests exist to observe revisions, and a missing row stays unavailable.

requests.cadence: FULL slots: first cycle, then every refresh_every_seconds (30 minutes)

required_per_attempt: received_at (UTC, microseconds, taken when the last body byte is read)
response body SHA-256 and byte length
logical_request_id linking the attempt to its manifest record
receipt_recording.existing_implementation: src/adapters/http_attempts.HttpAttemptLog (append-only index.jsonl, fsync per line, content-addressed bodies) and RawCaptureManifest.response_received_at inside the verified manifest hash.
receipt_recording.clock: One UTC wall clock per host, read by the collector through one injected clock that also stamps every request's attempt receipt. The collector does not measure NTP synchronisation; the runbook has the operator check it (w32tm /query /status) before the open and note the result with the session. Vendor row timestamps that postdate the local receipt are counted, never corrected; the normalizer's default tolerance is 0 ms.

recovery.missing_request: The failed attempt (transport error or non-2xx) is recorded in the cycle's attempt log; the cycle continues with its remaining requests; nothing is retried past the cycle boundary. The cycle is assembled with the endpoints it acquired and the failure is reported per cycle and per endpoint.
recovery.interruption: Every cycle is its own one-shot capture directory under <session>/cycles/<HHMMSS>/. A restart (--resume with the same session approval) reopens the session log; slots that passed during the gap are recorded MISSED_RESTART_GAP and collection resumes at the next future boundary. Gaps are reported by the assembler and the replay as decisions without availability; they are never backfilled from history or at_time endpoints, which carry no receipt for the historical instant.
recovery.partial_payload: A body that fails its manifest digest, or a response too large to read, is refused as a whole; no partial rows are normalized.
recovery.self_stop: The session stops itself after max_consecutive_failed_cycles cycles that acquired nothing, or when the one-shot reports AUTHENTICATION_REJECTED or STORAGE_FAILURE; the stop is logged and the summary written.

normalization_merge_rule.implementation: src/adapters/thetadata/session_assembly.py (assemble_session), on top of the unchanged single-capture normalizer research_events.normalize_capture with expected_endpoints and allow_unacquired
rule: Verify the session structure first: intent, session approval, schedule fingerprint, log, and every executed cycle's manifest, session id, scope, session date and approval against the log.

Normalize every executed cycle under the scope it was scheduled to issue; apply the single-capture rules inside each payload first (repeated identities grouped, identical duplicates coalesced, conflicts excluded whole).
Merge all cycles' records in recorded-availability order with the deterministic tie-break (available_at, cycle label, kind, key, event_at, row_index).

For each (kind, key, event_at) keep the CURRENT KNOWN REVISION. A record equal to it is a re-observation: not emitted, counted REOBSERVED_UNCHANGED; the original keeps its original availability and the event's age is never refreshed by re-observation.

A record that differs from the current revision is the next revision (sequence + 1) available at its own receipt. A -> B -> A yields three revisions; the final A is never discarded because it once appeared.

A new event_at is a new event with sequence 0, also when an older event_at arrives after a newer one (counted LATE_OLDER_EVENT); the replay's selection by (event_at, sequence) before validity is unchanged.

Each contract-list receipt is its own inventory event (event_at = receipt). Open interest and inventory acquired in a FULL cycle are reused between refreshes only through their own earlier availability; nothing is relabelled as observed in a later cycle, and a missing open-interest row stays unavailable.

An ambiguous (conflicting) observation revises nothing and revives nothing: the previously available state stands on its original receipt; the incident is counted AMBIGUOUS_AFTER_KNOWN_STATE or AMBIGUOUS_WITHOUT_KNOWN_STATE.

A MARKET cycle's option records are membership-checked against the latest listing available at their receipt (NOT_IN_LATEST_INVENTORY excluded, counted); before any listing is available they are retained and counted UNCHECKED_NO_INVENTORY_YET.

Every merged record's lineage names cycle, request_id, raw payload sha256, native row index, rule version and availability basis; the document's provenance names the session approval, the schedule fingerprint, the intent and log digests and every cycle's manifest.

futures.finding: None of the 66 pinned paths serves futures; the observed capture contains no futures contract, quote, size, tick size, point value or fee.
futures.action: Identify a futures source that records receive times before the pilot. Choosing or paying for one is an operational decision outside this repository; this file does not name a contract or a provider it has not inspected.

not_covered_by_this_specification: Any endpoint outside the pinned document.
Historical or at_time downloads as availability evidence.
Strategy, position, PnL or GEX computation.
operational_preconditions_validated: The one-shot refuses requests outside the market session window unless explicitly overridden; the schedule's first slot is the calendar open, 09:30:00 ET, inside that window, and no override is passed. The 09:29 ET first cycle proposed in v2.1.35 is corrected.
Bounded concurrency: one cycle in flight; an overrunning cycle is recorded, the slots it spans are MISSED_OVERRUN, and the next cycle starts at the next future boundary.

Raw request parameters (rate_value, annual_dividend) are recorded as wire values; a resolved economic rate and dividend yield need their own evidence before any GEX arithmetic. The assembler promotes neither.
